methodology: Deterministic scan of catalog/entries/ related: fields for slugs with no corresponding entry file. Script: playbooks/dangling-references/scripts/extract_dangling.py

consolidations.antifragility -> antifragile: Same concept, prefer adjective form as primary slug
consolidations.free-rider -> free-rider-problem: The problem framing is more useful for the catalog

candidates.name: Single Point of Failure
candidates.description: A component whose failure causes the entire system to fail. Widely applied from engineering to organizational design.

candidates.name: Analysis Paralysis
candidates.description: Overthinking a decision to the point of inaction. The analysis itself becomes paralyzing.

candidates.name: Antifragile
candidates.description: Systems that gain from disorder, going beyond resilience to actively benefit from stressors. Taleb's coinage.

candidates.name: Boundary Object
candidates.description: An artifact that means different things to different communities but enables coordination across boundaries.

candidates.name: Canary in a Coal Mine
candidates.description: An early warning indicator. From the mining practice of using canaries to detect toxic gases.

candidates.name: Feedback Loop
candidates.description: A system where outputs are routed back as inputs, creating self-reinforcing or self-correcting cycles.

candidates.name: 5S
candidates.description: Sort, Set in order, Shine, Standardize, Sustain. Workplace organization methodology from lean manufacturing.

candidates.name: Free Rider Problem
candidates.description: When individuals benefit from a shared resource without contributing. A core problem in collective action.

candidates.name: Impostor Syndrome
candidates.description: The persistent feeling of being a fraud despite evidence of competence. Incompetence as a hidden identity.

candidates.name: Normalization of Deviance
candidates.description: The gradual acceptance of rule violations when they don't immediately cause harm. Diane Vaughan's concept from the Challenger disaster.

candidates.name: OODA Loop
candidates.description: Observe, Orient, Decide, Act. Boyd's decision cycle for gaining advantage through faster iteration.

candidates.name: Planning Fallacy
candidates.description: The systematic tendency to underestimate time, cost, and risk of future actions. Kahneman and Tversky.

candidates.name: Psychological Safety
candidates.description: The shared belief that a team is safe for interpersonal risk-taking. Edmondson's concept, central to Google's Project Aristotle.

candidates.name: Resilience
candidates.description: The capacity to recover from disturbance and return to a functional state. Used across engineering, ecology, and psychology.

candidates.name: Signal to Noise
candidates.description: The ratio of useful information to irrelevant data. From electrical engineering, now ubiquitous in communication contexts.

candidates.name: Sky and Weather
candidates.description: Emotions are weather; the observing self is the sky. A mindfulness metaphor for separating identity from transient states.

candidates.name: Striking While the Iron Is Hot
candidates.description: Acting at the moment of maximum opportunity. From blacksmithing: metal is only workable when heated.

candidates.name: Sunk Cost Fallacy
candidates.description: Continuing an endeavor because of previously invested resources rather than future value. The fallacy of honoring irrecoverable costs.

candidates.name: Training Wheels
candidates.description: Temporary scaffolding that enables beginners to practice before full independence. From children's bicycles.

candidates.name: AI Alignment Is Training an Animal
candidates.description: AI alignment framed as animal training: reward shaping, behavioral conditioning, the gap between obedience and understanding.

candidates.name: Anchoring
candidates.description: The cognitive bias where initial information disproportionately influences subsequent judgments. The first number dropped anchors the negotiation.

candidates.name: Apocalypse
candidates.description: The archetype of total revelation through destruction. From Greek apokalypsis (unveiling), not merely catastrophe.

candidates.name: Applause Line
candidates.description: A line designed to trigger audience response. The theatrical machinery behind seemingly spontaneous agreement.

candidates.name: Argument from Authority
candidates.description: Claiming truth based on the speaker's status rather than evidence. Both a valid heuristic and a named fallacy.

candidates.name: Barn Raising
candidates.description: Community-coordinated collective construction. The archetype of mutual aid: everyone builds, everyone benefits.

candidates.name: Biodiversity Loss
candidates.description: The reduction of variety in a system, applied beyond biology to monocultures of thought, code, and organization.

candidates.name: Bounded Context
candidates.description: A boundary within which a domain model is consistent and meaningful. Eric Evans' DDD concept for managing complexity through explicit separation.

candidates.name: Brooks's Law
candidates.description: Adding people to a late project makes it later. Communication overhead grows quadratically with team size.

candidates.name: Burnout
candidates.description: Exhaustion framed as a fire that has consumed its fuel. The person-as-combustible-resource metaphor.

candidates.name: Chain of Command
candidates.description: Authority as a physical chain: each link connected to the next. Implies both connection and constraint.

candidates.name: Chain of Responsibility
candidates.description: A request is passed along a chain of handlers until one handles it. Gang of Four behavioral pattern.

candidates.name: Circuit Breaker
candidates.description: A mechanism that stops cascading failure by cutting the circuit when a threshold is breached. From electrical safety to software resilience.

candidates.name: Coming of Age
candidates.description: The narrative pattern of transition from innocence to experience. A threshold archetype applied to individuals, technologies, and fields.

candidates.name: Competitive Exclusion
candidates.description: Two species competing for the same niche cannot coexist indefinitely. Gause's principle, applied to markets and organizations.

candidates.name: Concentration of Force
candidates.description: Massing resources at the decisive point rather than spreading them evenly. Clausewitz's Schwerpunkt principle.

candidates.name: Confirmation Bias
candidates.description: The tendency to search for and interpret information that confirms existing beliefs. The mind as a biased filter.

candidates.name: Contrarian Thinking
candidates.description: Deliberately taking the opposing view to surface hidden assumptions. Thiel's question: what truth do few people agree with you on?

candidates.name: Conway's Law
candidates.description: Organizations design systems that mirror their communication structure. The org chart becomes the architecture diagram.

candidates.name: Cross-Pollination
candidates.description: Transferring ideas between domains, as pollen transfers between flowers. The mechanism behind analogical innovation.

candidates.name: Daemon Is a Background Spirit
candidates.description: Unix daemons named after Maxwell's demon: invisible agents doing work in the background. The supernatural origin of a technical term.

candidates.name: Dead Code
candidates.description: Code that exists but is never executed. Death as unreachability: the code is there but nothing can reach it.

candidates.name: Dead Man's Switch
candidates.description: A mechanism that activates when an operator becomes incapacitated. Safety through the absence of the expected signal.

candidates.name: Death by a Thousand Cuts
candidates.description: Failure from accumulated small problems rather than one catastrophic event. The Chinese lingchi torture as metaphor for cumulative degradation.

candidates.name: Decoy Effect
candidates.description: An inferior third option changes preference between two others. Asymmetric dominance: the decoy reframes the choice.

candidates.name: Diminishing Returns
candidates.description: Each additional unit of input produces less additional output. The fundamental curve that limits all optimization.

candidates.name: Divide and Conquer
candidates.description: Breaking a problem into smaller subproblems, solving each independently. From Roman imperial strategy to algorithm design.

candidates.name: Easter Egg
candidates.description: A hidden feature or message planted by creators for discoverers. The childhood hunt repurposed as insider delight.

candidates.name: Facade
candidates.description: A simplified interface to a complex subsystem. The building front that hides the plumbing. Gang of Four structural pattern.

candidates.name: First Mover Advantage
candidates.description: The advantage gained by being first to enter a market. Often overstated: fast followers frequently win.

candidates.name: Frankenstein
candidates.description: The creation that turns on its creator. Shelley's modern Prometheus: the hubris of making something you cannot control.

candidates.name: Gilding the Lily
candidates.description: Adding unnecessary embellishment to something already beautiful. From Shakespeare's King John: to gild refined gold.

candidates.name: Goedel's Incompleteness
candidates.description: Any sufficiently powerful formal system contains true statements it cannot prove. The fundamental limit of self-contained reasoning.

candidates.name: Goodhart's Law
candidates.description: When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure. The metric eats itself.

candidates.name: Grok
candidates.description: To understand something so thoroughly that you merge with it. Heinlein's Martian word for drinking-as-comprehension, adopted by hackers.

candidates.name: Groupthink
candidates.description: The deterioration of critical thinking in cohesive groups. Janis's concept: harmony becomes more valued than accuracy.

candidates.name: Hammer and Nail
candidates.description: When you have a hammer, everything looks like a nail. Maslow's law of the instrument: tools shape perception.

candidates.name: Hawthorne Effect
candidates.description: People modify behavior when they know they are being observed. The observer changes the observed.

candidates.name: Hedging Your Bets
candidates.description: Reducing risk by taking offsetting positions. From gambling hedges to financial derivatives.

candidates.name: Hero's Journey
candidates.description: Campbell's monomyth: departure, initiation, return. The universal narrative structure of transformation through ordeal.

candidates.name: Hit the Nail on the Head
candidates.description: To identify something exactly right. Precision as a single accurate blow.

candidates.name: Homeostasis
candidates.description: A system's tendency to maintain internal stability through self-regulation. Cannon's concept, applied far beyond physiology.

candidates.name: Information Overload
candidates.description: Too much information degrades decision-making. The mind as a system with finite carrying capacity.

candidates.name: KISS
candidates.description: Keep It Simple, Stupid. The design principle that simplicity should be a key goal. Kelly Johnson's Lockheed maxim.

candidates.name: Knowledge Is a Landscape
candidates.description: Understanding as spatial navigation: fields, frontiers, territories, exploration. Knowledge has terrain you can survey.

candidates.name: Ladder
candidates.description: Hierarchy and progress as vertical ascent. Career ladders, social ladders, ladders of abstraction.

candidates.name: Leverage Point
candidates.description: A place in a system where a small change produces large effects. Donella Meadows' twelve leverage points for intervening in systems.

candidates.name: Looking-Glass Self
candidates.description: We see ourselves through others' imagined perceptions. Cooley's concept: identity as a social mirror.

candidates.name: Murphy's Law
candidates.description: Anything that can go wrong will go wrong. Not pessimism but a design principle: assume failure modes will be exercised.

candidates.name: Mutualism
candidates.description: A symbiotic relationship where both species benefit. The cooperative counterpart to parasitism and competition.

candidates.name: Natural Selection
candidates.description: Differential survival and reproduction based on fitness. Darwin's mechanism, applied to ideas, companies, and code.

candidates.name: Pandora's Box
candidates.description: An action that unleashes irreversible consequences. The irretrievability of released forces, with hope trapped at the bottom.

candidates.name: Panning for Gold
candidates.description: Sifting through large quantities to find rare valuables. The prospector's patience: most of what you examine is worthless.

candidates.name: Parasitic Architecture
candidates.description: A system that attaches to and depends on a host system. Biological parasitism as architectural pattern.

candidates.name: Patina
candidates.description: The surface quality acquired through age and use. Wear as value: the opposite of pristine-as-good.

candidates.name: Predator-Prey
candidates.description: Coupled oscillations between hunter and hunted populations. Lotka-Volterra dynamics applied to markets, security, and evolution.

candidates.name: Prototype
candidates.description: A preliminary model built to test concepts before full investment. The disposable first attempt that teaches what to build.

candidates.name: Quis Custodiet Ipsos Custodes
candidates.description: Who watches the watchmen? Juvenal's question about recursive accountability in oversight systems.

candidates.name: Red Herring
candidates.description: A misleading clue that diverts attention from the real issue. From the alleged practice of using smoked fish to throw hounds off a scent.

candidates.name: Rupture and Repair
candidates.description: Relational breaks followed by reconnection strengthen bonds. The therapeutic concept that conflict, properly resolved, builds trust.

candidates.name: Scapegoat
candidates.description: The figure who bears the community's sins. From Leviticus: the goat sent into the wilderness carrying collective guilt.

candidates.name: Second-System Effect
candidates.description: The tendency to overdesign the second version of a system, loading it with features deferred from the first. Brooks's observation.

candidates.name: Servant Leadership
candidates.description: The leader exists to serve the team, inverting the traditional hierarchy. Greenleaf's model: authority through service.

candidates.name: Sharpening the Saw
candidates.description: Investing in maintaining and improving your tools and skills. Covey's habit 7: renewal as productive work, not indulgence.

candidates.name: Show, Don't Tell
candidates.description: Demonstrate through action and detail rather than stating directly. The fundamental craft rule for fiction, film, and presentations.

candidates.name: Siren
candidates.description: The irresistible lure that leads to destruction. From Homer's Odyssey: beauty as a trap requiring self-restraint.

candidates.name: Slippery Slope
candidates.description: A small concession leads inevitably to larger ones. Terrain as argument: once you start sliding, you cannot stop.

candidates.name: Sowing Seeds
candidates.description: Planting ideas or actions whose results emerge later. The agricultural patience: invest now, harvest in a different season.

candidates.name: Spike
candidates.description: A time-boxed investigation to reduce uncertainty. From railroad construction: driving a spike ahead to test the ground.

candidates.name: Staging Environment
candidates.description: A rehearsal space that mirrors production. Theater's dress rehearsal applied to software deployment.

candidates.name: Strange Loop
candidates.description: A hierarchy where moving through levels brings you back to the start. Hofstadter's concept linking Goedel, Escher, and Bach.

candidates.name: Strangler Fig
candidates.description: Gradually replacing a legacy system by growing a new one around it. Martin Fowler's pattern from tropical botany.

candidates.name: Straw That Broke the Camel's Back
candidates.description: A small addition that causes catastrophic failure in an already stressed system. The tipping point framed as accumulated burden.

candidates.name: Sugar-Coating
candidates.description: Making unpleasant information more palatable by wrapping it in pleasantness. The pharmaceutical origin: coating bitter pills.

candidates.name: Symbiosis
candidates.description: Close long-term interaction between different species. The umbrella concept for mutualism, commensalism, and parasitism.

candidates.name: T-Shaped People
candidates.description: Professionals with broad general knowledge (horizontal bar) and deep expertise in one area (vertical bar). IDEO's hiring metaphor.

candidates.name: Vestigial Structure
candidates.description: A feature that once served a purpose but now persists without function. The appendix of organizations and codebases.

candidates.name: When Pigs Fly
candidates.description: An impossibility marker. Adynaton: expressing disbelief through an image of the biologically absurd.

candidates.name: White Elephant
candidates.description: A possession more costly to maintain than it is worth. From the Thai royal gift: too sacred to use, too expensive to keep.

candidates.name: Whitewash
candidates.description: Concealing faults under a superficial layer of respectability. From the cheap lime paint that covers but does not repair.

candidates.name: Work in Progress
candidates.description: Inventory of unfinished items in a production system. From lean manufacturing WIP limits to kanban boards.
